arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: David Cortman argued for the sign owner. He said the town code discriminates based on what signs say. He said this violates the First Amendment.
Justice Roberts asked if political speech is more valuable than directions to a soccer game. He asked if this is fair.
Justice Alito asked if a yard sale sign has the same right as an election sign. He asked if this is fair.
Justice Kennedy asked if directional signs are a valid category. He asked if this is fair.

paragraphs: The case involves a town sign code. The code treats political signs differently from other signs. One side says this violates free speech. The other side says the town needs flexible rules to manage signs.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: The sign owner wants the Court to strike down the town sign code. The sign owner says the code violates free speech.
The town wants the Court to keep the sign code. The town says the code helps manage signs.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The sign owner says the town code discriminates based on what signs say. The sign owner says this violates the First Amendment.
The town says strict scrutiny would limit speech. The town says it needs flexible rules to manage signs.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Kennedy asked if a wealthy person can put up many birthday signs. He asked if this is like political signs.
Justice Ginsburg asked if birthday signs get the same treatment as political signs. She asked if this is fair.
